title: Can the lighter child balance?
hook: A 40 kg child on one side, a 20 kg child on the other. Can the lighter one ever win?

knows: seesaws balance with equal children at equal distances
weight in newtons is mass x 9.81
doesNotKnow: torque: turning effect = force x distance from the pivot
that balance needs equal torques, not equal weights

misconception: A seesaw balances only with equal weights, so a lighter child cannot balance a heavier one.
objective: The learner can explain that a seesaw balances when weight x distance is equal on both sides, so 20 kg at 4.0 m balances 40 kg at 2.0 m.

claims.text: A 20 kg child 4.0 m from the pivot balances a 40 kg child 2.0 m from it: each side turns the plank with 785 N·m.
claims.source: Torque = weight x perpendicular distance: 40 x 9.81 x 2.0 = 784.8 N m = 20 x 9.81 x 4.0 (artifacts/scratch/w4phys/check.mjs). Balance needs the torques about the pivot to cancel.

claims.text: What turns a seesaw is weight times distance from the pivot (torque), not weight alone; half the weight at twice the distance has the same turning effect.
claims.source: Rotational equilibrium: sum of torques about the pivot is zero (OpenStax University Physics Vol. 1, section 12.1 Conditions for Static Equilibrium). Archimedes' law of the lever.

claims.text: With unequal turning effects, a light rigid plank tips until one end touches the ground; it rests level only when the two sides are equal.
claims.source: A massless plank has no restoring torque of its own: any nonzero net torque rotates it until the ground stops it. Here pivot height 1.0 m and half-length 5 m give asin(1/5) = 11.5 degrees. The stage draws only level or fully tipped.

claims.text: Model: a light rigid plank pivoted at its middle, with each child treated as a single weight at one point.
claims.source: Stated on stage ('Light plank, pivot in the middle') and in the reveal. A uniform plank pivoted at its middle adds equal torques on both sides, so it would not change the 4.0 m answer.

claims.text: At the last spot other than 4.0 m that the learner slid to, the bars were unequal and one side went down: e.g. at 3.5 m, 687 N·m against 785 N·m, and the 40 kg side went down (stage: 'dashed: last tipped at 3.5 m, 687 N·m').
claims.source: 20 × 9.81 × 3.0 = 588.6 N·m < 40 × 9.81 × 2.0 = 784.8 N·m, so the net torque turns the 40 kg side down (sign of net in Demo.tsx). The reveal quotes the learner's last rested unbalanced spot (300 ms), or 3.0 m, where the child sits when the stage unlocks; beyond 4.0 m the 20 kg side goes down. Added v3 2026-10-14 by demo-builder. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): VERIFIED. 20 x 9.81 x 3.0 = 588.6 -> '589 N·m'; 40 x 9.81 x 2.0 = 784.8 -> '785 N·m' (toFixed(0)); net < 0 tips the 40 kg side down; beyond 4.0 m the 20 kg side. Demo `other` starts at 3.0 (on screen at unlock) and updates only after a 300 ms rest at a non-balanced spot, so the quoted spot was seen; every slider spot 0.5-5.0 gives the right side. | REOPENED 2026-10-14 (v4, wave E r6 revision by demo-builder): the reveal now quotes the learner's last unbalanced slider spot, kept on stage as a dashed bar. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 24): VERIFIED. Own node: 20 × 9.81 × 3.5 = 686.7 -> '687 N·m'; 40 × 9.81 × 2.0 = 784.8 -> '785 N·m'; net < 0 tilts the 40 kg (left) end down. 'tried-other' sets other on every non-4.0 move, so at reveal other is set and the dashed label 'dashed: last tipped at 3.5 m, 687 N·m' shows whenever d differs.

claims.text: Turning effect = kg × 9.81 × metres from the middle (in N·m).
claims.source: Torque about the pivot = weight × perpendicular distance = m g d with g = 9.81 m/s² (the plank's tilt is ignored for the comparison, as in the model; both sides scale by the same cos of the tilt). Stage caption above the torque bars. Added v3 2026-10-14 by demo-builder. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): VERIFIED. Torque about the pivot = m g d for a weight at horizontal distance d; tilt multiplies both sides by cos(theta), so the comparison is unchanged. kg x m/s^2 x m = N·m. Stage caption 'turning effect = kg × 9.81 × m from the middle' matches.

recall.question: A 30 kg child sits 1.0 m from a seesaw's pivot. How far out on the other side must a 10 kg child sit to balance?
recall.why: Balance needs equal weight x distance: 30 x 1.0 = 10 x 3.0. A third of the weight needs three times the distance.
